landmarks.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
landmarks.writeup: A stunning mosque in Muscat known for its grand architecture and the second largest hand-woven carpet in the world.

landmarks.name: Nizwa Fort
landmarks.writeup: A historic fort built in the 17th century, symbolizing Oman's rich heritage and strategic importance.

landmarks.name: Wahiba Sands
landmarks.writeup: A vast desert area famous for its red sand dunes and traditional Bedouin lifestyle.

landmarks.name: Jebel Akhdar
landmarks.writeup: A mountainous region known as the 'Green Mountain' with terraced farms and cool climate.

landmarks.name: Royal Opera House Muscat
landmarks.writeup: A premier venue for musical arts and culture, showcasing Oman's commitment to cultural development.

head_of_state: Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said

cultural_events.name: Muscat Festival
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event celebrating Omani culture, arts, and heritage with performances, crafts, and food.

cultural_events.name: Eid al-Fitr
cultural_events.writeup: A major Islamic festival marking the end of Ramadan, celebrated with prayers, feasts, and family gatherings.

cultural_events.name: Eid al-Adha
cultural_events.writeup: An important religious festival commemorating the willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son, observed with prayers and charity.

cultural_events.name: National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on November 18th, marking Oman's independence and unity with parades and cultural displays.

food_writeup: Omani cuisine features a blend of Middle Eastern, Indian, and African influences, with staples like rice, lamb, chicken, and seafood. Popular dishes include Shuwa (slow-cooked lamb), Majboos (spiced rice with meat), and Halwa (a sweet dessert).
brief_history: Oman has a history dating back to ancient times as a maritime power and trading hub. It was an important center for frankincense trade and later became a sultanate. Modern Oman was unified under Sultan Qaboos bin Said in 1970, leading to rapid modernization and development.

important_people.name: Sultan Qaboos bin Said (former ruler who modernized Oman)
Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said (current Sultan)
Sayyid Badr bin Hamad al Busaidi (Foreign Minister)

current_conflicts: Oman maintains a neutral foreign policy and is not involved in active conflicts. It plays a mediating role in regional disputes.
